text: Theoretical economics is a fundamental branch of economics. It studies the essential laws of economic phenomena through abstract theoretical models and mathematical tools, with a focus on exploring core issues such as resource allocation, market mechanisms, and economic growth from a logical perspective. Compared with applied economics, it pays more attention to theoretical derivation rather than the direct implementation of policies, providing a theoretical basis for various branches of economics (such as industrial economics, finance, and development economics). The major aims to cultivate academic talents with solid economic theory foundation, mathematical modeling ability and scientific research thinking, or compound talents who can engage in theoretical support work in fields such as policy research and financial analysis.
